_comment: Findings from the weekly analytics cycle, written by the routine described in agents/0_orchestrator.md's 'Weekly analytics cycle' section. Read by Agent 1.1/1.2 to weight future scouting toward what's working. Never used to adjust config/gates.json.

cycles.reason: state/posted_history.json is empty for both short_form and long_form — nothing has published yet, so there is no YouTube Data/Analytics API data to pull or summarize. This is expected on an early run: the short-form queue currently holds 5 scouted candidates (1 scripted: sf_001) from manual dry-run testing, none produced/gated/published; the long-form queue is empty.
cycles.scouting_guidance: None yet — first published items are needed before format/topic/style performance can be compared. Re-run this cycle after the shorts/long-form cycles have actually published something.

competitor_trend_research.method: Live web search (not YouTube Analytics — this is competitive/trend research, not this channel's own performance data) into what's currently working for other channels in the gym/discipline/motivation shorts niche, prompted by direct owner feedback that the pipeline's first two shorts were too slow-paced and used the wrong (calm ambient) audio for short-form.
findings: Aggressive phonk/hardtekk is the dominant trending audio style for gym/discipline/motivation shorts right now — not calm ambient. Specific trending flavors: 'Discipline Hardtekk' (hardtekk + phonk fusion), slowed/heavy-kick hardtekk mixes, aggressive phonk gym mixes. This matches the already-verified 'Phonk ish' (HoliznaCC0, CC0 1.0) track in state/cc0_audio_library.json — that track is correctly short-form-flavored and should be preferred for gym/discipline angles over the calm ambient tracks.

'Visual velocity' is the core editing principle for retention: something (a cut, punch-in zoom, new caption, sound hit) must change on screen every 1.5-3 seconds. Videos with dynamic text overlays and frequent cuts see meaningfully higher retention than static/single-shot content.
The hook must land in the first 2 seconds — most viewer drop-off happens immediately if the opening beat doesn't stop the scroll.
Captions/on-screen text carry the story for most viewers (a large majority watch with sound on but attention divided) — text must be legible and correctly sized, not an afterthought.

The 'dark gymcore' aesthetic — moody, low-exposure, high-contrast color grading — is a real, currently-trending visual style for gym/motivation content on TikTok/Shorts, not just a preference call. Baked into config/channel.json.short_form_style_guidance and scripts/short_form_transform.sh's default grade as of this research.
Format consistency matters for scaling: channels that keep a stable short-form structure (hook -> fast beats -> payoff) can iterate on hooks/topics without rebuilding editing workflow each time.
competitor_trend_research.action_taken: Updated config/channel.json (new short_form_style_guidance / long_form_style_guidance blocks), scripts/short_form_transform.sh (rewritten for multi-clip fast cuts, dark/low-exposure grade, safe auto-sized text), and agents/short_form/2.1_scriptwriter.md + 3.1_producer.md (fast-beat scripting, upbeat-audio-only rule, updated transform usage) to bake these findings into the pipeline going forward, not just this one fix.
competitor_trend_research.not_yet_done: Did not go back and re-produce/replace the already-published sf_001 (quarantined) or sf_002 (live) videos with the new fast-cut/upbeat-audio treatment — that's a call for the channel owner (replacing a live video is a real decision, not an automatic pipeline action).

direct_competitor_scan_2026_07_27.requested_by: channel owner, direct instruction to scan this specific channel's shorts
direct_competitor_scan_2026_07_27.method: YouTube channel pages are JS-rendered SPAs that don't come through static fetching, so used the channel's public RSS feed (youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=...) for real video listings, yt-dlp for per-video metadata (title/duration), and attempted yt-dlp media download for audio-track tempo analysis.
findings: Channel: 111K subscribers, ~2.2K videos, luxury lifestyle/supercars/motivation niche — very close analog to this channel's own niche and audience.

Several of this channel's own shorts (te1htnG3iI0, Jn8nw6bI2J0, 0k4KFkoEh4c, lCHBLevZK1c) are already saved in config/channel.json.reference_examples.short_form — this channel was already treated as a style reference before this scan.

Real duration data pulled via yt-dlp across 7 recent shorts: 24s, 17s, 14s, 10s, 24s, 12s, 9s — mostly well under 20s total, several near-minimum length, consistent with a very fast-cut editing style packing many short shots into a brief runtime.

Titles follow a simple repeating template: '[Rich/Luxury] [Life/Lifestyle/Vibes] 💰 #luxury #rich #money #motivation #millionaire #success #shorts #viral #lifestyle' — short, emoji-led, hashtag-heavy, not narrative titles.
direct_competitor_scan_2026_07_27.limitations_disclosed: Could NOT identify the exact song/artist used on their audio tracks — YouTube does not expose Content ID music attribution through public scraping (oEmbed, RSS, or yt-dlp metadata all came back empty for track/artist/album fields), and direct media download for tempo/waveform analysis was blocked with HTTP 403 (bot detection at YouTube's CDN, not a permissions issue we can fix). So the specific sound identity is unconfirmed — only structural findings (duration, cut-implied pacing, title pattern) are backed by real data pulled from the channel.
direct_competitor_scan_2026_07_27.action_taken: Owner separately specified clips should be capped at 2 seconds maximum per shot (their own direct observation, not derived from this scan's data, since exact cut timings weren't extractable either). Implemented as a hard requirement: rewrote scripts/short_form_transform.sh as scripts/short_form_transform.py, which now splits every short into <=2.0s shots (reusing clips with rotating offsets when there aren't enough distinct ones) regardless of how few/many clips are supplied. Updated config/channel.json.short_form_style_guidance and agents/short_form/3.1_producer.md to state the 2s cap explicitly as a hard ceiling, not just the general 1.5-3s visual-velocity range.

direct_competitor_scan_2026_07_27_pt2.requested_by: channel owner, follow-up instruction: 'deeply analyse' this channel and build a list of 25 sounds it uses, since YouTube blocked exact sound extraction in the first scan.
direct_competitor_scan_2026_07_27_pt2.method: YouTube's own audio blocking held: retried yt-dlp with web/tv/ios player clients specifically to work around the earlier android_vr 403 — web client returned 'Requested format is not available' (needs a PO token this environment can't generate), tv client falsely reported 'DRM protected' (a known yt-dlp/YouTube quirk for some Shorts, not a real DRM restriction), ios client hit 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot'. Also parsed the Short's raw ytInitialData JSON directly (not just WebFetch's markdown conversion) looking for musicVideoType/trackTitle/artistNames/audioTrack fields — none present for Shorts via the web renderer. Concluded YouTube's Content-ID audio attribution is genuinely inaccessible from this environment via any available method, and stopped retrying rather than risk further bot-detection escalation.
direct_competitor_scan_2026_07_27_pt2.pivot: This channel is also on TikTok as @millionaire_mentality_7 (found via the first scan's web search). TikTok's yt-dlp extractor DOES return real `track`/`artists` fields per video via `yt-dlp --dump-json --skip-download --flat-playlist --playlist-end N "https://www.tiktok.com/@millionaire_mentality_7"` — confirmed working, pulled 400 videos' worth of metadata.

sound_list_25.honesty_note: Of 33 distinct `track` values found across 400 videos, the large majority are TikTok's own generic per-repost label (e.g. 'original sound', 'orijinal ses', 'suara asli', 'som original', 'suono originale' — these are the same generic label in different languages, crediting whichever account's upload/duet chain the sound is attributed to, NOT a real song title). These are real data pulled from the channel, but do not identify an actual song — only that some sound exists and which account TikTok currently credits it to. Marked below as [generic]. Only entries marked [identified] are genuine song/artist names.

4. [ambiguous] "fancy" — artist shown only as a symbol; likely references a known 'Fancy' track (Iggy Azalea or similar) but could not be confirmed, not counted as identified

Gata Only NJ / gata only remix — derivative edits of 'Gata Only' by FloyyMenor & Cris MJ (viral 2024/2025 hit)
sound_list_25.takeaway_for_pipeline: Only ~6-7 of these 25+ are genuinely identifiable songs, and none are confirmed CC0/license-free — they're mainstream/viral tracks (Ice Spice, CKay, Indila, Gata Only, Danza Kuduro) that would need a CC0 substitute, same as every other cycle. The clearest actionable signal: Brazilian funk/phonk 'montagem'-style production (DJZRX/motty/rodricci circle) appears twice independently, reinforcing that aggressive Brazilian-phonk-adjacent production is a real, recurring choice for this niche — consistent with the already-verified 'Phonk ish' CC0 track already in use. The 'generic original sound' majority is itself a finding: a lot of this channel's audio is opportunistic reuse of whatever's currently trending, re-attributed by repost chains, not a curated original soundtrack — not something a CC0-only pipeline can replicate 1:1 regardless of scraping effort.
